notes: The copula goes to the prepositional predicate כְּאִיּוֹב (rule 49), reading מִי as the clause's subject; the competing reading makes מִי the predicate and takes the *is*, as rule 20's מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה does.
גֶּבֶר is a written antecedent with no relative morpheme beside it, so *Who* is added (rules 46, 55).
